title: Integration discovery: SDK & Proxy feasibility - Luthien Systems
summary: Initial integration discovery focused on SDK fit, gateway/proxy pattern, LangChain/LlamaIndex usage, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer leaning toward dedicated but needs private options and KMS/audit assurances. Agreed to run a pilot with a small dedicated pool and LangChain test harness.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Rate limits, quotas and throttling behavior
Security: KMS, SOC2, VPC/private control plane
action_items: Maya - Share dedicated pricing breakpoint spreadsheet by 2026-03-16
Diego - Provide sample LangChain prompt adapter and a small test repo link by 2026-03-18
Hannah - Send list of compliance questions (SOC2/ISO/SAML) to Redwood by 2026-03-13
next_steps: Redwood to run latency/cost baseline with customer's sample prompts and return numbers
Customer to provision sandbox VPC peering details for private plane review if pilot succeeds
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sofia Park (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (CTO, Luthien), Omar N'Golo (Lead Platform Eng), Hannah Lee (Security), Samir Bose (NLP Eng)
Shared artifacts: intro deck (link: https://redwood.example/decks/luthien-intro), sample prompts spreadsheet, request for compliance doc noted

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you blocking time. Quick intros, then we'll jump into how you're thinking about integrating with Redwood.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Thanks Maya. We're trying to evaluate options for serving our internal and B2B features. Key constraints are latency under 250ms p95 for small chat completions, strict data residency, and audit logs for regulators.
[00:33] Maya Chen: Got it. Diego and Sofia are on to go deeper on the technical fit. Diego, do you wanna start with the SDK story?
[00:39] Diego Alvarez: Sure. Hi all. Redwood's SDKs are REST + first-class Node/Python clients, and we have a lightweight gateway proxy pattern for on-prem or hybrid setups. For LangChain/LlamaIndex, we provide adapters and a small example repo — it's basically a thin layer so you can plug in our SDK as a backend.
[00:58] Samir Bose: When you say adapters, are those maintained by Redwood or community-maintained? We have a few custom prompt chains and retrievers using LlamaIndex.
[01:08] Diego Alvarez: Good question — basic adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex are Redwood-maintained and updated with runtime changes. For heavy customizations we recommend keeping your own wrapper but we try to keep the adapter surface stable.
[01:20] Omar N'Golo: How does the gateway/proxy pattern work exactly? We have an edge gateway and want to avoid double-encrypting or exposing keys.
[01:29] Sofia Park: The pattern we often recommend is a lightweight sidecar proxy that handles auth and rate-limiting, and forwards calls to Redwood's hosted or dedicated endpoints. For Private deployments you can run a local control plane and connect to your VPC. Sidecar can be deployed as a k8s DaemonSet or as a standalone service.
[01:46] Priya Shah: We're leaning toward Dedicated or Private because of data residency and audit logs, but cost is a factor. Can you explain the dedicated reserved capacity model and burst behavior?
[01:57] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with a baseline throughput and optional burst capacity. Pricing has a reserved commit and then overage per token. We can show you the breakpoint spreadsheet — Diego will attach typical numbers.
[02:10] Priya Shah: And failure modes? If dedicated capacity is saturated, do you fail open to hosted?
[02:18] Diego Alvarez: It's configurable. You can set a fallback policy to route to a lower-cost hosted variant or to a cheaper quantized model. For regs we usually keep a hard limit and queue requests; for consumer features teams sometimes opt for a soft fallback to hosted for uptime.
[02:30] Hannah Lee: For compliance, we need KMS integration and customer-controlled key material. Is HSM/KMS supported? Audit log granularity?
[02:38] Sofia Park: Yes — Private + Dedicated both support KMS integration. Private gives you the most control — customer-managed KMS and optional HSM. Audit logs include per-request metadata, token counts, model version, route, and requestor id. We can provide a sample schema.
[02:52] Priya Shah: Great. Samir, any initial thoughts on LangChain/LlamaIndex integration?
[02:58] Samir Bose: Two quick things — we use LlamaIndex for embedding + vector store and LangChain for orchestration. Need to understand rate limit semantics per API key and how batching of embeddings is supported. Also how does caching work for KV cache in decoder context?
[03:14] Diego Alvarez: For embeddings we support batch endpoints with configurable batch size; onboarded models expose a batch size recommendation. For decoding we rely on KV cache optimizations in our runtime — that's internal, but from the SDK perspective, large chat contexts can be prefetched and we expose cache-control headers for prefix caching.
[03:31] Omar N'Golo: Are those cache-control headers something our proxy can set to take advantage of prefix reuse?
[03:36] Sofia Park: Exactly. Your sidecar can tag requests with a conversation id and prefix hash; the runtime will use it to route to same cache shard when possible. It reduces token compute cost and improves latency.
[03:48] Priya Shah: On rate limits — can we set per-tenant quotas within Dedicated? We need per-customer quotas for our multi-tenant offering.
[03:57] Maya Chen: In Dedicated you can define per-api-key quotas and rate-limit rules; we also support hierarchical quotas (per-tenant under an org) via the gateway. The sidecar can enforce soft rate-limits before requests hit the pool.
[04:09] Priya Shah: Any gotchas with long tail latencies when batching for embeddings? We don't want spikes in p99.
[04:16] Diego Alvarez: Balancing batching and latency is workload-specific. Our Optimize tooling suggests batch configurations per workload and offers an autoscaling policy that keys off queue depth and tail latency. For embeddings, we recommend smaller batch sizes with parallel workers to avoid p99 spikes.
[04:31] Hannah Lee: About observability — we use OpenTelemetry internally. What traces/metrics do you export and can we ingest them into our telemetry backend?
[04:40] Sofia Park: We support OTEL traces and Prometheus metrics. We export spans for request lifecycle, per-token timing, model selection, routing decisions, and batching windows. You can forward to your backend or use Redwood Console.
[04:54] Omar N'Golo: Do you provide correlation IDs so that we can tie logs to our requests?
[04:58] Diego Alvarez: Yes, there's a request-id header and we recommend passing an x-correlation-id. The system surfaces this in traces and logs.
[05:06] Samir Bose: For LlamaIndex, we sometimes do local embedding compute and then store vectors remotely. Can we POST embeddings and then call the generation endpoint with a retriever id?
[05:16] Sofia Park: You can ingest vectors via the embeddings API and then reference them in generation calls via retriever metadata. We also have an experimental sparse retrieval interface — but that's beta.
[05:26] Priya Shah: Security question — do you have SOC 2 Type II? How about SAML/SSO and RBAC for the console?
[05:34] Maya Chen: Yes SOC 2 Type II; SAML SSO and SCIM as well as RBAC with fine-grained permissions are supported. We'll send the compliance pack.
[05:43] Hannah Lee: Please include retention policies and data deletion proofs — our auditors ask for that.
[05:48] Maya Chen: Noted. Hannah, if you can send the exact list we'll prioritize.
[05:52] Priya Shah: How fast is the SDK rollout? We have devs using Python and Node. We also have a Go backend, any client there?
[06:00] Diego Alvarez: Official SDKs for Python and Node; community-maintained Go client exists and we can provide examples. For LangChain we have a Python adapter; LlamaIndex examples are Python-first.
[06:10] Omar N'Golo: If we run a dedicated pilot, what's the typical timeline to provision a small pool?
[06:15] Sofia Park: For a small dedicated pool it's usually 7-10 business days for capacity provisioning and network setup, shorter if we use hosted with VPC peering for Private review.
[06:24] Priya Shah: Any options for a hybrid where we keep sensitive requests on Private and route lower-sensitivity to Hosted?
[06:30] Diego Alvarez: Yes — that's a common pattern: smart routing by policy. We support region and sensitivity-based routing, and you can set model variants per policy for cost controls.
[06:40] Samir Bose: Let's talk about cost controls quickly — how do you measure per-token and attribute costs? We need to show engineering the cost per feature.
[06:48] Maya Chen: Redwood Console breaks down token-level costs by route, model, and API key. You can also set alerts on cost velocity. The Optimize toolkit provides suggestions like quantizing models for dev traffic to cut costs.
[07:01] Priya Shah: If we do pilot, we want a very small SLA for latency and a rollback plan.
[07:07] Sofia Park: We'll propose an SLA for the pilot window and a canary rollout strategy; we can do automatic fallback to hosted variants if latency increases beyond thresholds.
[07:16] Maya Chen: Quick process note: I'll share the pricing spreadsheet and a sample pilot scope. Diego will share the LangChain/LlamaIndex repo and a small sandbox manifest for the sidecar. Hannah will share compliance items.
[07:29] Priya Shah: Sounds good. Omar — any infra constraints on your side for peering?
[07:33] Omar N'Golo: We'll need firewall rules and a static egress IP list. Also we prefer TLS mutual auth for service-to-service calls.
[07:41] Diego Alvarez: Mutual TLS is supported in Private deployments; for Dedicated we can do a VPN + mTLS depending on the networking plan. We'll include network requirements in the kickoff doc.
[07:51] Samir Bose: One last technical: do you expose model hyperparameters like temperature/penalty and support function calling?
[07:58] Sofia Park: Yes — full generation parameters exposed, streaming, and function/tool calling are supported. For function calling we also provide structured output validation helpers.
[08:10] (cross talk)
[08:14] Priya Shah: Let's recap next steps. Maya?
[08:17] Maya Chen: Recap: share pricing sheet (Maya), LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo + sidecar manifest (Diego), compliance Qs from Hannah, schedule pilot kickoff — target 2026-03-23. We'll aim to provide baseline latency/cost numbers within 5 business days of getting the sample prompts.
[08:38] Priya Shah: Thanks. Appreciate the clarity.
[08:41] Omar N'Golo: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up on peering and firewall list.
[08:45] Hannah Lee: I'll email the compliance checklist by Friday.
[08:48] Maya Chen: Great — I'll send notes and links. Thanks all.

End of transcript
